sections.label: Community mediation framework strengthened
sections.summary: The Bill strengthens community mediation and lets authorised officers direct disputing neighbours to Community Mediation Centre mediation.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: First, the Bill will strengthen the community mediation framework.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: It will empower authorised officers to direct disputing neighbours to attend mediation at the Community Mediation Centre.

sections.label: Dedicated Community Relations Unit
sections.summary: The Bill proposes setting up a dedicated Community Relations Unit, or CRU.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Second, the Bill proposes the setting up of a dedicated Community Relations Unit, or CRU in short.

sections.label: CDRT powers and processes
sections.summary: The Bill enhances the powers and processes of the Community Disputes Resolution Tribunals, or CDRT.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Third, Sir, the Bill enhances the powers and processes of the Community Disputes Resolution Tribunals, or CDRT in short.

sections.label: Neighbour noise feedback received
sections.summary: Over the past three years, public agencies received more than 90,000 pieces of feedback on neighbour noise alone.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Over the past three years, public agencies have received more than 90,000 pieces of feedback on neighbour noise alone.

sections.label: Neighbour noise feedback resolved
sections.summary: Today, around 90% of neighbour noise feedback is resolved after grassroots, community leaders or HDB officers helped both sides compromise.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Today, around 90% of neighbour noise feedback is resolved after grassroots and other community leaders or HDB officers helped both sides to reach an amicable compromise.

sections.label: Directing parties to mediation
sections.summary: Authorised officers will be empowered to direct disputing neighbours to attend mediation at the CMC in appropriate cases.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: We want all suitable cases to go through an amicable mediation in the first instance.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: We will, therefore, empower authorised officers to direct disputing parties, the neighbours, to attend mediation at the CMC in appropriate cases.

sections.label: Offence for non-compliance
sections.summary: Failure to comply without reasonable excuse is an offence.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Failure to comply, without reasonable excuse, will be an offence.

sections.label: CMC mediators neighbour cases
sections.summary: Since 2014, CMC mediators have helped make peace between neighbours in over 2,400 cases.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Since 2014, CMC mediators have helped to make peace between neighbours in more than 2,400 cases.

sections.label: Registering settlement as CDRT order
sections.summary: Parties can register a settlement agreement as a CDRT order if both consent, allowing enforcement through the CDRT process.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Parties who come to a settlement can opt to register their settlement agreement as a CDRT order if both parties consent.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Thus, if one party to the agreement breaches the settlement terms, assuming it is registered, then the other party can quickly proceed to use the simplified CDRT process to enforce the settlement agreement in the same way as a CDRT order.

sections.label: Setting up dedicated CRU
sections.summary: After public consultations, it was decided to set up a dedicated CRU for stronger levers in these cases.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: In our public consultations, Singaporeans have generally agreed that we need stronger levers to act decisively and effectively in these types of cases.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: We have decided, therefore, to set up a dedicated CRU.

sections.label: CRU noise sensors consent
sections.summary: Under new sections 13I and 13J, the CRU may deploy noise sensors with consent to collect objective evidence of noise events.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Under the new sections 13I and 13J, the CRU may also leverage on technology and deploy noise sensors, with consent, to collect objective evidence of noise events.

sections.label: CRU focus on severe cases
sections.summary: The CRU will focus only on severe neighbour noise cases causing disamenity and severe hoarding cases.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: The CRU will focus its resources only on severe neighbour noise cases that are causing disamenity to the community and also severe hoarding cases.

sections.label: CRU pilot in Tampines
sections.summary: The CRU is intended to be piloted first in the HDB estate of Tampines town.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: As such, we intend to, first, pilot the CRU in the HDB estate of Tampines town.

sections.label: Mediation before CDRT claims
sections.summary: New section 18A requires residents to attempt mediation before filing a CDRT claim, as over 70% of claimants had not first tried CMC mediation.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: First, under the new section 18A, there will be a general requirement that residents must first attempt mediation before filing a CDRT claim.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: This ensures that neighbours do not take each other to the CDRT, without at least first trying mediation.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: We do this, because when we look back at our cases, in the last five years, more than 70% of CDRT claimants indicated that they did not first attempt CMC mediation, before filing a CDRT claim.

sections.label: CRU information disclosure to CDRT
sections.summary: Under new sections 13I(4) and 13J(4), the DG of CRU and CRU officers may disclose information gathered in their work to the CDRT.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Next, under new sections 13I subsection 4, and 13J subsection 4, the DG of CRU and CRU officers may disclose information gathered, in the course of their work, to the CDRT.

sections.label: CDRT Mandatory Treatment Orders
sections.summary: Under new section 12A, the CDRT will be empowered to issue a Mandatory Treatment Order, or MTO.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Third, under the new section 12A, the CDRT will be empowered to issue a Mandatory Treatment Order, or MTO for short.

sections.label: CDRT Interim Orders
sections.summary: Under new section 5A, the CDRT may issue Interim Orders on a prima facie threshold if unreasonable interference is likely to continue or substantially affect the claimant.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Next, under the new section 5A, the CDRT will be empowered to issue Interim Orders on a prima facie threshold if the acts of unreasonable interference are likely to continue, likely to have a substantial adverse effect on the claimant, or his day-to-day activities, and it is just and equitable for an interim order to be made.

sections.label: Tenant-occupied property notifications
sections.summary: New section 10A lets residents experiencing unreasonable interference from a tenant-occupied property notify the landlord, who has oversight responsibility.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Next, the new section 10A, addresses tenant-occupied properties.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: They have a responsibility to exercise some oversight on their tenants' conduct.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Hence, under the new section 10A, residents who experience unreasonable interference from a tenant-occupied property can notify the landlord.

sections.label: Landlord bond for tenant compliance
sections.summary: The CDRT can require a landlord to put up a bond to secure his tenant's compliance with a CDRT order.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Concurrently, the CDRT can require the landlord to put up a bond to secure his tenant's compliance with the CDRT order.

sections.label: DG of CRU applying to CDRT
sections.summary: Under new section 17A, the DG of CRU may apply for a dispute to be heard by the CDRT if necessary to preserve community peace.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Under the new section 17A, the DG of CRU may apply for a dispute to be heard and determined by the CDRT, if satisfied that this is necessary in the interests of preserving the community peace.

sections.label: Civil restraint orders for unmeritorious claims
sections.summary: Under new sections 31B to 31E, the CDRT will be empowered to make civil restraint orders against unmeritorious claims.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: In such cases, sometimes parties may exploit the simple low-cost process and commence unmeritorious claims and sometimes repeatedly so.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Therefore, under the new sections 31B to 31E, the CDRT will be empowered to make civil restraint orders.

sections.label: Balancing intervention and neighbour responsibility
sections.summary: The passage calls for balancing intervention with empowering neighbours, and notes MSO hosting a unit and HDB piloting Mediation Directions.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Ultimately, this is delicate work, as I mentioned earlier, to balance between intervening too much with the framework that allows us all these measures of relief, but also empowering neighbours themselves to take ownership and responsibility of their own difficulties, their own neighbourly problems and resolve them themselves.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Ultimately, I call on all Members to help us, through our interactions with our residents, to build a gracious society, where neighbours are conscious of their roles in the community, to exercise mutual consideration for one another, and where differences are best bridged through discussion and compromise, and not necessarily by direction or order.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: First, the Municipal Services Office (MSO) will host the dedicated unit to address severe neighbour noise and hoarding cases.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Second, HDB, which helps to manage neighbour noise disputes within HDB flats today, will pilot the early issuance of Mediation Directions by frontline officers.

sections.label: Abatement order to stop noise
sections.summary: If Mr Y persists, the DG of Community Relations may issue an abatement order under new section 13L directing him to stop the noise.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: If Mr Y persists with his actions, then the DG of Community Relations may issue an abatement order under the new section 13L and direct Mr Y to stop the noise.

sections.label: Penalty for breaching abatement order
sections.summary: Failure to comply with an abatement order is a criminal offence punishable by a fine or imprisonment, or both.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Failure to comply with an abatement order will be a criminal offence, punishable by a fine or imprisonment, or both.

sections.label: Noise sensor deployment conditions
sections.summary: Noise sensors are deployed only after CROs and ACROs narrow the unit, and only with consent under new section 13I(1).

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: First, noise sensors will be deployed only after CROs, assisted by ACROs, have done initial investigations and narrowed down the unit where the noise might be coming from.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Second, noise sensors will only be deployed with consent, as laid out under the new section 13I, subsection 1.

sections.label: Real-time data transmission
sections.summary: To prevent tampering, raw sensor data is transmitted in real-time to Singapore-based servers for processing.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Third, to prevent tampering, raw data that is collected by the sensors will be transmitted in real-time to Singapore-based servers for processing.

sections.label: HDB compulsory flat acquisition
sections.summary: Clause 36 amends section 63 of the Housing and Development Act to empower HDB to compulsorily acquire a flat.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: We may consider referring the case to HDB to consider compulsory acquisition if all other levers have failed to abate the nuisance and measures are required to protect the wider community.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Therefore, clause 36 of the Bill amends section 63 of the Housing and Development Act to empower HDB to compulsorily acquire a flat.

sections.label: Decluttering hoarded residential units
sections.summary: Clause 11 inserts new section 11A into the CDRA, empowering the DG to apply to CDRT to declutter a residential unit.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: To better address severe in-unit hoarding, clause 11 of the Bill inserts a new section 11A into the CDRA.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: The provision empowers the DG to apply to CDRT to declutter a residential unit, as a measure of last resort premised on public interest and only after existing regulatory levers from frontline agencies have been exhausted.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: The DG may apply to the CDRT for an order to address hoarding, under the new section 11A, after the CDRT has found the hoarder to be causing unreasonable interference to the hoarder's neighbour and the hoarder has failed to comply with the CDRT's order to declutter.

sections.label: Initial team and operations timeline
sections.summary: An initial team of officers is developing operational procedures, with operations hoped to begin in the second quarter of 2025.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: We have formed the initial team of officers, who are working on developing their operational procedures.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: We hope to begin operations from the second quarter of 2025.

sections.label: CRU Tampines pilot and powers
sections.summary: The CRU is piloted in Tampines for one year, with CROs issuing mediation directions, warnings, abatement orders, or applying for MTOs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: To lay a solid foundation for the CRU, we have decided to pilot it in Tampines for one year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: For neighbour noise disputes that can potentially be resolved through mediation, CROs can issue mediation directions to expedite the resolution process.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: For cases that cannot be resolved by mediation, CROs can investigate these cases and issue warnings, abatement orders, or apply for court-ordered MTOs.

sections.label: Planned operations start 2025
sections.summary: Guided by these principles, operations are planned to commence in the first half of 2025.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Guided by these principles, we plan to commence operations in the first half of 2025.

sections.label: Compelled mediation at Community Mediation Centre
sections.summary: Mediation often fails when one party refuses to attend, but compelled attendance at the Community Mediation Centre gives at least a 70% chance of resolution.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Frequently, many efforts to resolve quarrels between neighbours fail right at the start because one party simply refuse to attend the mediation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: But if parties are compelled to attend mediation at the Community Mediation Centre, at least there is a 70% chance, or higher, that the dispute may be resolved.

sections.label: Mediators, neutral environment, hoarders' treatment orders
sections.summary: Experienced mediators say speaking in a neutral environment helps resolve disputes, and the Bill's powers include mandatory treatment orders for hoarders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Experienced mediators tell me, that getting parties to speak to each other in a neutral environment helps very much in resolving disputes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: I also support the powers given under the Bill to deal with hoarders, which include the powers to make a mandatory treatment order.

sections.label: CDR Act not a silver bullet
sections.summary: The speaker said in 2015 that the CDR Act is not a silver bullet, and says the amendments are also not a silver bullet.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: The Police may knock on his doors late at night and he may face hostility from simply one complainant.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: I have said, in 2015, when the Bill was enacted that this CDR Act is not a silver bullet which will resolve all neighbour disputes – and Minister Edwin Tong says it, too.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: I would say that, the amendments to this Bill is also not a silver bullet that will solve all neighbour disputes.

sections.label: Golden rule and private disputes
sections.summary: The golden rule of reciprocity should apply, and the Government is urged to consider that not all neighbour disputes are private.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: The golden rule or the rule of reciprocity should apply, "Do unto others what you want them to do unto you".

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: I do urge the Government to consider that not all disputes between neighbours are private disputes.

sections.label: CRU to be set up in Tampines
sections.summary: The speaker hears with excitement that the CRU will be set up in Tampines.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: First, I hear with excitement that the CRU will be set up in Tampines.

sections.label: Noise sensor privacy assurance
sections.summary: A Member urges the Government to assure residents that their privacy is protected so they will allow noise sensors to be installed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: If I heard correctly, Senior Minister of State Sim Ann has said that the equipment will not record every conversation made by the residents in the household.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: So, let me urge the Government that it is important to assure residents that the privacy of residents is protected and if there is no such assurance that privacy will be protected, residents are unlikely to allow the noise sensors to be installed.

sections.label: Initial team size and scaling
sections.summary: A Member asks the Minister for details on the initial team's size and the Government's plan to scale it up.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Like Mr Lim Biow Chuan before me, can the Minister share some more details regarding the size of the initial team and what is the Government's current plan to scale up from the initial team?

sections.label: Appointment of CROs
sections.summary: Proposed section 13C lets the DG appoint a Police Officer, a public officer, or a Statutory Board officer or employee as CROs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: The proposed section 13C allows the DG to appoint three types of personnel to be CROs: one, a Police Officer; two, a public officer; and three, an officer or employee of a Statutory Board.

sections.label: Entering homes without consent
sections.summary: A Member asks in what circumstances officers will enter homes to collect evidence without flat owners' consent.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Regarding entrance to residences, may I ask in what circumstances will officers enter homes to collect evidence without the need for consent from flat owners?

sections.label: Noise sensor deployment locations
sections.summary: A Member seeks clarification on whether noise sensors will be deployed in the complainant's flat or in common corridors and areas.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Regarding the deployment of noise sensors by CRU officers, I know that consent is required of the owner of the affected unit.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: I wish to seek a clarification from the Minister whether the authorities expect the deployment of sensors to be within the complainant's flat or even in common corridors or other common areas.

sections.label: Mediation and mediated settlement terms
sections.summary: The Bill allows the CRU and CMC to direct parties to mediation, and mediated settlement terms will carry the force of a Court order.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Indeed, MinLaw shared in its paper in this Bill on 24 August 2024 that less than 30% of total cases registered at the CMC proceed to mediation because one party does not wish to participate in mediation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: The Bill will also allow the CRU and the CMC to direct parties to attend mediation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: I say this because many residents are still reluctant to proceed to CDRT due, among other reasons, to the formal requirements imposed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: This will carry the same force and effect as an order of Court.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Allowing mediated settlement terms to have the weight of an order of Court will ensure greater compliance by both parties to the mediated settlement terms to ensure better and longer-term resolution of their disputes.

sections.label: Mediation cases and outcomes
sections.summary: Of 1,200 to 1,900 cases from 2021 to 2023, under 30% went to mediation, but over 80% of those were amicably resolved.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In the reply, I note that out of the 1,200 to 1,900 cases received from 2021 to 2023, less than 30% of such cases proceeded to mediation, but for the cases that had, more than 80% were amicably resolved after the mediation.

sections.label: Mediation Direction by CRO
sections.summary: New section 13M of the Bill provides for a Mediation Direction issued by a CRO to parties in a complaint or dispute.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The new section 13M of the Bill provides for a Mediation Direction that can be issued by a CRO to parties involved in a complaint or dispute.

sections.label: CDRT enforcement orders and compliance
sections.summary: From January 2021 to December 2023 only 14 CDRT enforcement orders were made, showing high compliance, though residents may not pursue proceedings due to perceived cost and tedium.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: As shared by the Ministry, between January 2021 to December 2023, there are only 14 enforcement orders made by the CDRT.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: This shows the high rate of compliance with CDRT orders.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: However, as shared by the Ministry, despite the effectiveness of CDRT, similar to the CMC route, many residents might not choose to pursue CDRT enforcement proceedings even if they have valid grounds to do so, due to the perception of cost and tedious process involved in this legal avenue.

sections.label: Support for CRU and mediation directions
sections.summary: Despite CMC's 80% mediation success rate, voluntary mediation deters residents, so the speaker supports the CRU issuing mediation directions to mandate disputing parties to accept mediation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Although CMC has a high mediation success rate of 80%, many residents are unwilling to participate due to the voluntary nature of mediation, making it difficult to thoroughly resolve issues.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Therefore, I support the establishment of CRU, which gives them the authority to issue mediation directions, mandating disputing parties to accept mediation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: This will help encourage more residents to participate in mediation and prevent disputes from escalating. : Mr Speaker, in conclusion, I believe that the Community Disputes Resolution (Amendment) Bill has the potential to resolve community disputes more efficiently and amicably by ensuring mediation and empowering public servants in the new CRU to address complex cases.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: By piloting and eventually scaling up the CRU with public servants given the appropriate authorities, ensuring safeguards in mandatory psychiatry treatment order and promoting CDRT as a final resort, while ensuring the enforceability of CDRT orders, will all contribute to residents being able to benefit from more resolved disputes and having a positive experience through the process.

sections.label: Fees for devices under section 13H
sections.summary: This is stated in new section 13H, and the speaker asks whether the homeowner will be charged a fee for using these devices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This is stated in the new section 13H.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: However, I would like to ask whether the homeowner will be charged any fee for the use of these devices.

sections.label: HDB advice on kitchen tap leaks
sections.summary: In highlighted cases HDB advised a neighbour not to use the kitchen tap, but the advice was not heeded, worsening the leak; HDB advises affected residents to seek compensation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Some of the cases that I highlighted are situations where HDB conducted visits and advised the neighbour not to use the kitchen tap in the kitchen sink, but this advice is not heeded by the homeowner, which caused the leak to worsen and cause more damage to the property of the neighbour below.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I understand that HDB will advise affected flat residents to contact their neighbours and seek compensation for damages incurred or medical costs.

sections.label: Expanding CDR Act to commercial units
sections.summary: Suggests future CDR Act amendments cover commercial units in HDB blocks, not just residential units, since tribunal dispute resolution may not address root causes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Here, I would like to suggest that future amendments to the CDR Act is further expanded to include commercial units located in HDB blocks, not just residential units alone.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The resolution of disputes between neighbours through the tribunal process may not be a permanent solution if the root cause or main issue is not addressed.

sections.label: Mediation and neighbour noise dispute framework
sections.summary: Describes enhancements to mediation, CDRT powers, and the neighbour noise dispute framework, including mandatory mediation, CRU investigations, noise sensors, and registering settlements with CDRT.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: One, is the enhancements to the mediation process and the processes and powers of CDRT; and, two, the framework for neighbour noise dispute resolution for high-rise living.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: I welcome the proposed enhancements to the mediation framework to allow CMC or the proposed new CRU to make mediation mandatory.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: The proposed amendments also gives the CRU authority to investigate severe noise nuisance cases, including the ability to order noise sensors to be placed in homes and to get objective evidence of noise levels to issue warnings or abatement orders.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: The proposed enhancements will also allow neighbours who have reached a mediation settlement to register the agreement with CDRT.

sections.label: Enhanced CDRT processes and powers
sections.summary: States the amendments enhance CDRT processes and powers, letting it consider CRU evidence, issue interim orders, and issue MTOs for those with mental health conditions causing disturbances.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: The proposed amendments also enhances the CDRT processes and gives it more power.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: This will allow the CDRT to consider relevant evidence that CRU officers have gathered, issue interim orders facilitating faster relief as well as MTOs for those believed to be causing disturbances due to mental health conditions.

sections.label: CRU pilot and HDB acquisition powers
sections.summary: Asks whether the one-year Tampines CRU pilot will assist severe cases in other towns and private apartments, and what safeguards prevent abuse of CRU and HDB compulsory acquisition powers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: As the proposed CRU will be a pilot that will run for a year starting with Tampines, I would like to seek clarification on whether CRU will also be available to assist with severe cases in other towns and those living in private apartments facing severe neighbour disputes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Because if we do, then it really means that society and neighbourly relations are really breaking down.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: These include the new CRU with the authority to investigate cases, including the ability to order noise sensors to be placed in homes to get objective evidence of noise levels and to issue warnings or abatement orders.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: At the same time, the amendments will also enable HDB to compulsorily acquire any HDB dwelling where the owner or authorised person has been convicted of an abatement offence or exclusion offence.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: So, I do like to ask the Senior Minister of State, what measures will be put in place to safeguard against the abuse and ensure that the powers are exercised appropriately?

sections.label: Compliance bonds for landlords
sections.summary: States landlords may be required by the Court to put up compliance bonds of up to $20,000, forfeited if tenants fail to comply with CDRT orders.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Landlords may be required by the Court to put up compliance bonds, where up to $20,000 may be forfeited if their tenants fail to comply with orders of the CDRT.

sections.label: CRU, CDRT and HDB powers
sections.summary: Notes the changes concern the CRU, CDRT processes, and HDB's increased powers, and expresses disappointment that the CRU pilot runs only in Tampines for one year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: These relate to the CRU, the CDRT processes and HDB’s increased powers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: It is somewhat disappointing that the CRU, which will have powers of intervention on the ground, will only be activated in Tampines Town on a one-year pilot.

sections.label: HDB compulsory acquisition abatement offence
sections.summary: Clause 36 would let HDB compulsorily acquire a flat if an owner or related authorised occupier is convicted of an abatement offence with a prior record.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Clause 36 of the Bill proposes to enable HDB to compulsorily acquire a flat if the owner or an authorised occupier related to the owner is convicted of an abatement offence and has a prior record of another abatement or exclusion offence.

sections.label: Family after below-market compensation
sections.summary: The question asks how a family will move on given that compulsory acquisition results in below-market compensation being paid to owners.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Given that compulsory acquisition will result in a below-market compensation being paid to the owners, how will the family move on from here?

sections.label: CDRT cases 2015 to 2019
sections.summary: Earlier Parliamentary Questions' answers show 380 cases were filed with the CDRT from 2015 to 2019.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Based on the answers to earlier Parliamentary Questions, we know that 380 cases were filed with the CDRT from 2015 to 2019.

sections.label: CDRT and CMC mediation rates
sections.summary: Minister Shanmugam shared in 2019 that CDRT made a mandatory mediation order in 25% of cases, and under 30% of CMC cases proceed to mediation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Minister Shanmugam previously shared in 2019 that the CDRT has made a mandatory mediation order in 25% of the cases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Further, I have read that less than 30% of the total cases registered at the CMC proceed to mediation.

sections.label: Concurrent coverage and 2025 start
sections.summary: The question asks whether it can be covered concurrently, noting the Senior Minister of State said it would start as soon as the second quarter of 2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The question is, whether it can be covered concurrently?

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: I know that the Senior Minister of State has mentioned that it would start as soon as second quarter of 2025.

sections.label: Educating CROs and ACROs
sections.summary: Since new section 13F makes CROs and ACROs public servants under the Penal Code, they must be educated on sections 161 to 165 offences.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: As the new section 13F provides that CROs and ACROs will be considered “public servants” under the Penal Code, it is necessary to properly educate them on the offences under sections 161 to 165 of the Penal Code so that they do not inadvertently commit an offence by accepting any gift or token of appreciation from grateful residents after helping to resolve any community dispute.

sections.label: CDRT order and public official function
sections.summary: Section 11A lets the CRU seek a CDRT order to declutter a residential unit where the resident is unwilling or unable despite a notice or advisory.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: With the new section 11A, the CRU can apply for a CDRT order to declutter a residential unit where the resident is unwilling or unable to do so despite a notice or advisory by a CRO, a public officer, an officer or employee of a Statutory Board or a person exercising a public official function.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Would a grassroots advisor or MP be "a person exercising a public official function", who can issue the notice or advisory to remove or dispose of clutter?

sections.label: Resident disputes low value items
sections.summary: A resident may view certain items as not of low or no value or utility, a precondition for a CDRT order under section 11A.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: For example, the resident may take the view that certain items are not "of low or no value or utility", which is a precondition for a CDRT order under the new section 11A.

sections.label: HDB compulsory flat acquisition powers
sections.summary: Part 3 grants HDB powers to compulsorily acquire a flat if the owner or authorised occupier meets requirements including conviction of an abatement or exclusion offence.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: One of the most significant and attention-grabbing provisions in this Bill are in Part 3, which grants HDB new powers to compulsorily acquire a flat if the owner, or a specified authorised occupier, has, amongst other requirements, been convicted of an abatement offence or exclusion offence under the Community Disputes Resolution Act.

sections.label: Compulsory acquisition conviction thresholds
sections.summary: Clause 36 allows compulsory acquisition only if the owner or occupier was convicted of at least two abatement or exclusion offences, or one compounded or taken into consideration.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Based on HDB, CMC and CDRT's analysis of past cases, how many cases of compulsory flat acquisition can we expect in a given year?

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Under clause 36 of the Bill, compulsory acquisition is only allowed if the owner or occupier has been convicted of at least two abatement offences or exclusion offences, or had at least one other abatement offence or exclusion offence which was either compounded or taken into consideration for sentencing.

sections.label: HDB compensation policy factors
sections.summary: Minister Desmond Lee said HDB's compensation policy for compulsorily acquired flats considers factors including severity of infringement, case circumstances, and administrative and holding costs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In a Parliamentary reply in October 2022, Minister Desmond Lee told the House that "HDB's compensation policy for flats that are compulsorily acquired takes into account various factors, including the severity of the infringement and the circumstances of the case, as well as the administrative and holding costs in acquiring the flat.

sections.label: CRO powers and selection criteria
sections.summary: The Bill expands CRO powers to issue abatement orders and enter residences, and clause 13C requires CROs to be public officers, police officers, or statutory body employees.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: While I support the Bill, I would like to raise some points for further clarification and offer a few suggestions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This Bill significantly expands the powers of CROs, empowering them to issue abatement orders and, in certain cases, to enter residences to help address serious disturbances.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: First, regarding selection criteria: clause 13C of the Bill specifies that CROs must be public officers, police officers, or statutory body employees.

sections.label: Mediation attendance and interference scope
sections.summary: Asks whether measures ensure meaningful engagement in mediation and whether acts outside clause 4(2) categories remain actionable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Given the Minister's clarification that the Bill makes it an offence not to attend mediation, are there measures to ensure that respondents not only attend but engage meaningfully in the mediation process?

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: While the amendments provide additional detail, with clause 4(2) specifying types of interference covered, I would like to confirm whether acts or omissions outside these categories are still actionable, or if the scope has been intentionally narrowed.

sections.label: Compelling parties to attend mediation
sections.summary: About 70% of registered cases cannot be resolved because parties refuse to take part, so compelling attendance is expected to increase cooperation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Presently, about 70% of registered cases cannot be resolved because one or more parties refuse to take part.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: With legislation compelling all parties to attend mediation when directed by the authorised agencies, we can expect better communication and clearer understanding of one another’s issues and perspectives, increasing the chances of cooperation and compromise to resolve disputes.

sections.label: Subjective criteria for rest hours
sections.summary: Asks how the Ministry will assess and recommend where criteria are subjective, such as differing rest hours due to shift work.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Residents may have different rest hours due to shift work.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Hence, I would like to ask the Ministry how it will make assessments and recommendations where the criteria is subjective and convince all parties that it is being fair and even-handed?

sections.label: Agency readiness for increased demand
sections.summary: Asks whether agencies are ready to cope with increased demand on their resources.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Are our agencies ready to cope with the increased demand on their resources?

sections.label: Hoarding task force progress
sections.summary: Asks for the progress and challenges of the Hoarding Task Force and Hoarding Management Core Group and lessons gleaned.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Could the Minister clarify the progress and challenges of the inter-agency Hoarding Task Force and Hoarding Management Core Group thus far, and what lessons have been gleaned in the past?

sections.label: First MTO escalation pathway
sections.summary: States this is the first time an MTO is introduced as an escalation pathway to community disputes under the Act.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: To my knowledge, and I stand advised, this is the first time we are introducing the construct of an MTO as part of an escalation pathway to community disputes, specifically and directly as part of the Act.

sections.label: MTO in this Act
sections.summary: Asks why the Ministry included an MTO in this Act and how it differs from a CPC MTO.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Could the Minister share with us why the Ministry has opted for the inclusion of an MTO in this Act specifically, and how its application will be distinctive, or otherwise, from the MTO ordered under the CPC?

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: If it is the case that a person is so recalcitrant to the extent of egregious public nuisance or non-adherence to Court orders, even under the influence of mental illness, would that not then constitute as an offence that could be sentenced under community orders or MTO anyway, under the current CPC framework?

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: And if it is the case that the CRO is already authorised, with or without consent, to remove items of public risk and concern, as proposed under the new section 11, is this not sufficient to address and then resolve the community dispute, rather than adding on a further amendment and order for the person to be sentenced to mandatory treatment?

sections.label: Autonomy over treatment
sections.summary: Argues that if unreasonable interference is resolved, it should remain the individual's choice whether to seek treatment.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: If the central concern of dispute, which as articulated in the Act, is an "unreasonable interference" in relation to a neighbour of an individual, if it has been addressed and mitigated sufficiently, it should still remain within the autonomy of the individual whether to seek treatment for his or her condition.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We can encourage, we can help the person see reason for treatment and we can facilitate such a possibility, but to make it legally mandatory and enforceable is something rather different in my view.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: If a person, notwithstanding his or her mental disorder, adopts a position that still resolves the "unreasonable interference" but does not wish to seek treatment, should that not be respected and be considered acceptable, even as we consider the challenging situations in the context of the proposed amendments?

sections.label: CDRT mandatory treatment orders
sections.summary: States the CDRT is empowered to issue an MTO to a person with a mental health condition causing nuisance.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: One of the key enhancements to the CDRT is to empower it to issue a MTO to a person believed to be suffering from a mental health condition leading to acts of nuisance.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: This person will need to undergo a mandatory assessment and/or treatment.

sections.label: HDB flat compulsory acquisition
sections.summary: States HDB may consider compulsory acquisition of flats in severe recalcitrant cases, a recourse unavailable in private estates.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Next, for cases occurring in HDB estates, HDB has the option to consider the compulsory acquisition of flats in the event of severe recalcitrant cases, where all other measures have failed.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: However, this recourse is not available in private estates.

sections.label: Noise feedback and CRU powers
sections.summary: States HDB noise feedback rose and the CRU will be empowered to take calibrated action including mediation and noise sensors.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim
sentences.text: Numbers showed that from January to September 2020, HDB received 11,400 cases of feedback relating to noise, an increase of about 3,600 cases for the same period in 2019.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim
sentences.text: Under the proposed amendments, the proposed CRU will be empowered to take targeted, calibrated action in certain cases.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim
sentences.text: Besides warnings and orders, the CRU will have the ability to mandate mediation and deploy noise sensors within dwellings to collect objective data.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim
sentences.text: Importantly, less than 30% of the current neighbourhood dispute cases proceed to mediation, indicating that an increased focus on resolution is needed, and consultation has shown broad support for these measures among advocacy groups and community leaders.

sections.label: Tribunal mandatory treatment orders
sections.summary: States the Bill empowers the Tribunal to issue mandatory treatment orders for extreme nuisance behaviours possibly caused by mental health conditions.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim
sentences.text: The Bill will also empower the Tribunal to issue mandatory treatment orders, recognising that some extreme behaviours that cause nuisance to others may be the result of a mental health condition.

sections.label: Mandatory eviction consequences for residents
sections.summary: The speaker says mandatory eviction's consequences must be considered, particularly residents who could face homelessness or insecure housing.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim
sentences.text: While I agree that property owners must take responsibility, we must consider the potential consequences of mandatory eviction, particularly for residents who could, subsequently, face homelessness or insecure housing.

sections.label: Support for vulnerable property owners
sections.summary: The speaker asks how the Ministry will provide support and guidance to property owners, especially vulnerable populations, to navigate these requirements.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim
sentences.text: Can the Ministry explain how they will provide support and guidance to property owners, especially vulnerable populations, to navigate these requirements?

sections.label: Noise dispute violent confrontation case
sections.summary: The speaker cites an October 2023 CNA case where a noise dispute escalated to a violent confrontation with a wooden pole and kitchen knife after three years.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim
sentences.text: To illustrate this point, I note a case reported in October 2023 by CNA, where a noise dispute between neighbours escalated to a violent confrontation involving a wooden pole and a kitchen knife after three years of tension.

sections.label: Mediation compliance beyond existing fine
sections.summary: The speaker says granting agencies power to mandate mediation attendance is a step forward but calls for enforceable measures beyond the existing $1,500 fine.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: Granting agencies, like CRU and CMC, the power to mandate mediation attendance is an important step forward.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: However, we must also go further to ensure compliance with clear, enforceable measures beyond the existing $1,500 fine.

sections.label: Registering settlement agreements at CMC
sections.summary: The amendment permits parties to register their settlement agreements at CMC, giving them the same force as a CDRT order.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: The amendment permits parties to register their settlement agreements at CMC, giving them the same force as a CDRT order.

sections.label: Calibrating compliance bond for landlords
sections.summary: The speaker says the compliance bond may be insufficient if too low versus rental income, proposing calibration to rental fees or revoking rental privileges.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: This is a necessary step to prevent escalation of such issues.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: However, the proposed compliance bond for landlords may not be sufficient if the bond amount is too low in comparison to rental income.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: To enhance its deterrent effect, may I propose for consideration, calibrating the bond amount to reflect rental fees or revoking the landlord's rental privileges for a set period of time if the issues persist.

sections.label: Community mediation success rate
sections.summary: Community mediation resolves 80% of voluntary cases, but only 30% of disputes proceed to mediation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: An effective tool for resolving such disputes amicably is through community mediation, which has a high success rate, with 80% of voluntary mediation cases resulting in mutual compromise.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Despite this, currently, only 30% of disputes proceed to mediation, often because one party is unwilling to participate.

sections.label: CDRT last-resort powers
sections.summary: The Bill gives the CDRT new powers, including expedited interim orders and bonds requiring landlords to ensure tenant compliance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: For a minority of cases that are particularly severe and cannot otherwise be resolved, the CDRT will act as a last-resort avenue for complainants after mediation and failed interventions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: This Bill will enhance the CDRT with new powers to facilitate quicker and more effective resolution of cases, including issuing interim orders on an expedited basis, such as to remove an obstruction from the common corridor or to stop making excessive noise.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Landlords will also be encouraged to take a more active role when their tenants cause nuisance, as the CDRT can order tenants to cease the nuisance and require landlords to ensure compliance through a bond.

sections.label: Noise feedback during pandemic
sections.summary: Noise feedback rose during the pandemic and remains unabated, with over 2,100 monthly cases in the first half of 2024.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Indeed, public feedback on noise climbed during the pandemic and remains unabated – the first half of 2024 saw an average of more than 2,100 monthly cases, more than five times that of 2019; and it is high.

sections.label: Clarifications on Bill execution
sections.summary: The Member seeks clarifications on execution, noting CMC mediation succeeds in about 80% of voluntary cases but only 30% proceed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: For intended outcomes to be better achieved, I seek clarifications on several areas of this Bill, especially in the area of execution, as good policy requires good execution for the benefits of this Bill to be effective on the ground.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I note the new measures in this Bill appears to be based on past learnings that CMC mediation has been effective, where about 80% of voluntary mediation cases at CMC have been successful.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: But only a small proportion of about 30% of registered cases proceed to mediation due to a majority of residents refusing to do so.

sections.label: CRU pilot in a town
sections.summary: Clause 14 proposes a one-year CRU pilot in a town to address severe neighbour noise and hoarding cases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Next, on the introduction of the CRU pilot to address severe neighbour noise and hoarding cases, as proposed in clause 14 of the Bill, I note the plans to do a one-year pilot in a town.

sections.label: CDMF enhancements for residents
sections.summary: Cases yearly since the pandemic are over five times 2019 levels, and the Member welcomes measures giving residents faster relief.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: On average, from the pandemic till now, cases every year is more than five times that of 2019.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Having consistently advocated for enhancements to the CDMF over the last four Budgets and COS debates, I welcome these new measures that provide faster and more effective relief for residents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: An updated CDMF is essential in resolving conflicts peacefully by addressing the root causes of disputes.

sections.label: Unity and good neighbourliness
sections.summary: The passage calls for opening hearts, mutual understanding and respect to resolve disputes and maintain unity, and states support for the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: We should open our hearts, foster mutual understanding and come together as good neighbours to resolve dispute.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: It is through greater mutual respect and empathy, building harmony and diversity that we maintain the spirit of unity. : Mdm Deputy Speaker, notwithstanding these clarifications, I support this Bill.

sections.label: Amendment to Community Disputes Resolution Act
sections.summary: The passage says legal means are exhausted, welcomes a proposed amendment, and notes a CRU would get powers to direct mediation and install noise sensors after neighbours fail to resolve disputes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: So, quite clearly, we have, from the current legal standpoint, exhausted available means to resolve the situation in our neighbourhood.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I am therefore glad to know that the Government is now considering an amendment to the Community Disputes Resolution Act so that we have more legal muscle to help our residents who have been suffering from such measures and my other colleagues before me.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In a statement released by MCCY and MND, it was highlighted that the CRU that will be set up would be given powers to issue direction for neighours to attend mediation and install sensors to collect data on noise.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: These actions, however, will be taken only after the neigbours have failed to resolve disputes amongst themselves.

sections.label: Managing alleged offenders
sections.summary: The passage states alleged offenders could be compelled to attend mediation, ordered to mandatory treatment for mental health conditions, or have their flats acquired as a last resort.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I do understand that there are several ways in which alleged offenders could be managed under the proposed new framework.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: They could be compelled to attend mediation; they could be ordered to attend mandatory treatment if it is believed that they are causing disturbance due to mental health conditions; and in the most extreme situation, flats of the alleged offenders could be acquired as a last resort if they are recalcitrant and/or the nuisance created is very severe.

sections.label: CDMF and its enhancements
sections.summary: The passage states the CDMF and its enhancements hopefully strengthen community-based resolution and promote good neighbourliness.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: The CDMF and its enhancements do hopefully represent a significant step forward in strengthening our community-based resolution and promote good neighbourliness overall.

sections.label: Landlords and tenants' behaviour
sections.summary: The passage notes many Yio Chu Kang seniors rent out HDB flats for income and asks whether landlords should be held accountable for tenants' behaviour.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: In Yio Chu Kang, many seniors rely on renting out their HDB flats to supplement their income.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: While maintaining peace is critical, is it fair to hold landlords accountable for their tenants' behaviour?

sections.label: Mediation agreements later breached
sections.summary: The passage asks the Ministry for data on CMC mediation sessions resulting in agreements later breached and whether such cases are tracked.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Could the Ministry provide data on how many mediation sessions in the CMC have resulted in agreements that were later breached?

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Is there a tracking mechanism for such cases?

sections.label: Resident proposals on CRU pilot
sections.summary: A resident welcomes the Bill and CRU pilot, urges scaling beyond Tampines, and proposes landlord guidance, mental health support, MCST clarity, CRO training, and accessible mediation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Residents eagerly anticipate the launch of the CRU pilot, which adds support to earlier interventions may fall short.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I hope to see this pilot scale beyond Tampines to other areas, including Yio Chu Kang, to benefit more residents with unresolved disputes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Our communities welcome the initiatives in this Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: However, as always, the devil is in the details.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I urge the Minister to consider my proposals in my speech.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: First, provide guidance to landlords on preparing tenancy agreements and related documents to comply with this Bill, offer mental health support for hoarding cases to prevent recurrence, clarify the roles of MCSTs and officers' authority in private properties, ensure adequate training and safeguards for CROs and lastly, make mediation more accessible and guarantee swift enforcement.

sections.label: Appointment of non-officer ACRO
sections.summary: Under new sections 13C and 13D, an individual who is not a Police officer, public officer or Statutory Board employee may be appointed an ACRO.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Under the new sections 13C and 13D, an individual who is not a Police officer, public officer or an employee of a Statutory Board may be appointed an ACRO.

sections.label: Monitoring data use restriction
sections.summary: New section 13X provides that any monitoring data collected must only be used for performing duties under the Act.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The new section 13X provides that any monitoring data collected must only be used for performing duties under the Act.

sections.label: Tribunal and DG order powers
sections.summary: Under new sections 11A and 13L, a tribunal and the DG may make orders or authorise officers to exercise powers with or without owner or occupier consent.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Under the new sections 11A and 13L, a tribunal and the DG have powers to make orders or authorise officers to exercise powers with or without the consent of the owner or occupier.

sections.label: Second-hand smoke survey results
sections.summary: Out of 2,510 families surveyed, 1,183 reported experiencing second-hand smoke in their homes one to three times daily.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Out of 2,510 families surveyed, 1,183 reported experiencing second-hand smoke in their homes one to three times daily.

sections.label: Ineffective enforcement legal order
sections.summary: The passage asks what purpose a legal order serves if enforcement is ineffective and citizens are left without protection.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: What purpose does a legal order serve if enforcement is ineffective and citizens are left without protection?

sections.label: Court order against neighbour smoking
sections.summary: The family obtained a Court order for the neighbour to cease smoking, but it was to no avail.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In this unfortunate case, it surfaced that the family had obtained a Court order for the neighbour to cease the smoking, but to no avail again.

sections.label: Solutions for second-hand smoke
sections.summary: The question asks what solutions the Government is studying for second-hand smoke in homes and whether CRU can focus on such disputes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can the Minister share what solutions the Government is studying to address second-hand smoke in homes and whether CRU can also focus on neighbourly disputes on second-hand smoke?

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: If not now, then, whether there is a timeline to include this?

sections.label: CRO volunteering and free CRU services
sections.summary: CROs and ACROs may volunteer in their own time if it does not clash with public duties, and CRU services and authorised sensor deployment are free.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: But for avoidance of doubt, CROs and ACROs can, of course, like public officers, choose to volunteer in their own time, as long as it does not clash with their public duties.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: Also, CRU services to the public and the deployment of sensors that have been authorised by CRU are free of charge.

sections.label: CROs investigate escalated noise cases
sections.summary: CROs and ACROs will investigate cases escalated to CRU to uncover root causes of neighbour noise disputes, and sound thresholds are not intended now.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: CROs and ACROs will be empowered to investigate cases that are escalated to the CRU, so that the root causes of neighbour noise disputes may be uncovered, the parties concerned are brought together to address these root causes and, where necessary, the appropriate action is applied and/or support given, as the case may be, to the correct party.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: To Mr Mark Lee's question on introducing sound thresholds or time-based guidelines, we do not intend to do so at this time.

sections.label: CRU discretion under section 13K
sections.summary: For such cases, section 13K gives the CRU discretion not to investigate or take further action.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: For such cases, section 13K gives the CRU discretion not to investigate or take further action.

sections.label: Expunging raw sensor data
sections.summary: Raw data picked up by the sensors will be expunged once it is processed.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: Raw data picked up by the sensors will be expunged once it is processed.

sections.label: CRU officer composition
sections.summary: The CRU comprises 15 full-time dedicated public officers trained in investigation and basic mediation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: The CRU currently comprises 15 full-time dedicated public officers trained in investigation and basic mediation.

sections.label: CRO unit entry conditions
sections.summary: Under section 13L, CROs may enter a unit to seize items only if a written warning, abatement order and two written warnings were issued and not complied with.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: Under section 13L, CROs may only enter a unit to seize items if: a written warning was previously issued to the individual; and that written warning was not complied with, and an abatement order was issued; and the abatement order was not complied with; and at least two written warnings were issued to the individual to comply with the abatement order.

sections.label: Questions on flat acquisition criteria
sections.summary: Ms Hazel Poa and Mr Alex Yam asked about criteria for compulsory acquisition of flats for nuisance makers, expected cases, and fairness as a last resort.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: Ms Hazel Poa and Mr Alex Yam asked about the criteria for compulsory acquisition of flats for nuisance makers, and Ms Poa also asked on the number of expected cases and how the Government will ensure that the measure is exercised fairly and only as a last resort.

sections.label: No acquisition for mental health
sections.summary: The Government does not intend to implement compulsory acquisition of flats where mental health conditions or special needs are involved.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: To the question raised by Ms Sylvia Lim and other Members, we do not intend to implement compulsory acquisition of flats where mental health conditions or special needs are involved.

sections.label: CRU focus and compensation framework
sections.summary: CRU will focus on the underlying cause of noise nuisance, and HDB's prevailing compensation framework applies to compulsory acquisition under clause 36 amendments.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: As far as possible, CRU will focus on addressing the underlying cause for the noise nuisance.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: And to Ms Hazel Poa's query on compensation, HDB's prevailing compensation framework will apply to the compulsory acquisition of flats which are undertaken pursuant to the amendments under clause 36 of this Bill.

sections.label: CRU mental health training
sections.summary: CRU officers will be trained to identify persons with mental health needs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: CRU officers will be trained to identify persons with mental health needs.

sections.label: Enabled Living Programme pilot
sections.summary: Changes may involve daily routine and care arrangements, and MSF's upcoming Enabled Living Programme pilot may help persons with disabilities and special needs live in the community.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: These may, for example, involve changes to the person's daily routine and care arrangements.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: We hope that initiatives, such as MSF's upcoming Enabled Living Programme pilot, can help more persons with disabilities and special needs live and thrive within the community.

sections.label: Growth in hoarding cases
sections.summary: The number of hoarding cases has shown a clear growth trend over the years and the causes can be complex.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: Over the years, there has been a clear growth trend in the number of hoarding cases and the causes can be complex.

sections.label: Conditions for forced decluttering order
sections.summary: The DG can apply for a forced decluttering order only after the CDRT finds unreasonable interference, advisories are issued, the CDRT orders decluttering, and the hoarder refuses to comply.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: The DG can only apply for a forced decluttering order after the CDRT has found the hoarder to be causing unreasonable interference to his neighbour, advisories to declutter have been issued to the hoarder and the CDRT ordered the hoarder to declutter, but the hoarder refused to comply with the Court order.

sections.label: CRU handling of after-hours cases
sections.summary: The CRU will not attend immediately to after-hours cases as such disputes are usually not emergencies, and will process them the next working day.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: The CRU will not attend immediately to cases reported after hours, because neighbour noise or hoarding disputes are not usually emergencies that require immediate intervention.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: CRU will, on the next working day, process cases that were received after hours the day before and arrange to visit the affected parties as soon as practicable.

sections.label: Piloting the CRU model
sections.summary: The CRU model will be piloted and reviewed, with pilot operations hoped to commence in the first half of 2025, and subsidiary legislation and operational processes worked on after the Bill passes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: We seek your patience for us to pilot the CRU model and review it carefully to ensure that our processes are effective and that manpower needs for expansion of coverage are sized correctly.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: We hope to commence pilot operations in the first half of 2025.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: After this Bill is passed, we will continue working on the subsidiary legislation and firm up operational processes.

sections.label: CRU role and pilot scope
sections.summary: The CRU tackles severe noise and hoarding disputes where amicable resolution is exhausted, and only the CRU is piloted while mediation and CDRT enhancements apply once the Bill is operational.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: The CRU's role is to tackle the severe noise and hoarding neighbourly disputes that are out there, where prior attempts at amicable resolutions have been exhausted and where there is serious disamenity to the community.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: The vast majority of cases can and should be addressed through better dialogue between neighbours and community self-help.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Ms Joan Pereira asked about neighbour disputes outside of the CRU pilot.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: I want to emphasise that it is only the CRU that is being piloted.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: The framework, as regards mediation as well as the enhancements to the CDRT, is not the subject of the pilot and they apply the moment the Bill is operational.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: But to Ms Pereira's question, residents who stay in private estates or in HDB estates outside of the CRU pilot areas, will, therefore, still benefit from the enhancements to the mediation and CDRT framework.

sections.label: Second-hand smoke complaints share
sections.summary: In 2023, second-hand smoke made up 0.6% of total NEA-related complaints.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: In 2023, the last numbers, second-hand smoke comprised 0.6% of the total number of NEA-related complaints.

sections.label: CDRT seizure case withdrawal
sections.summary: In the seizure case, the CDRT claim was filed in October 2021 and withdrawn in January 2022 after a settlement agreement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: In the seizure case, the CDRT claim was filed in October 2021.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Three months later, in January 2022, the claimant withdrew the application on the basis that the claimant had reached a settlement agreement.

sections.label: Smoking ban enforcement application dismissed
sections.summary: In the other smoking ban case, the claimant applied to enforce the order but the CDRT dismissed it in April 2023 for lack of demonstrated breach.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: In relation to the other case where there was also an order to ban smoking – I think Mr Louis Ng referred to that – the claimant in that case did, as Mr Louis Ng said, apply to enforce the order.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: But at the hearing before the CDRT, the claimant was unable to demonstrate that there was a breach of the order and, therefore, the enforcement application was dismissed in April 2023.

sections.label: PA trained GRLs mediation
sections.summary: As of October 2024, the People's Association has trained over 500 GRLs in basic mediation skills.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: As of October 2024, the People's Association (PA) has trained over 500 GRLs in basic mediation skills.

sections.label: Removal of $5 fee
sections.summary: From January of next year, the payment of the $5 fee will be removed so that it is entirely free.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: There might be a different point of view.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: And as I said, from January of next year, we will remove the payment of the $5 fee so that it is entirely free.

sections.label: CMC duty mediators appointed
sections.summary: CMC has appointed 30 experienced duty mediators to manage directed mediation cases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: CMC, as I said, has been preparing for this.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: It has appointed 30 experienced duty mediators to manage directed mediation cases.

sections.label: Breached settlement agreements data
sections.summary: The government does not track the number of cases where settlement agreements are subsequently breached.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: To Mr Yip Hon Weng's question on the number of cases where settlement agreements are, thereafter, breached, we do not track this data.

sections.label: CMC administrative fee removal
sections.summary: From 1 January, the CMC's $5 administrative fee will be removed to promote voluntary mediation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
