sentences.text: Mr Derrick Goh also mentioned the CMC's $5 administrative fee, as I said, with effect from 1 January, we will remove this and we hope that this will further promote the use of voluntary mediation to resolve disputes earlier.

sections.label: Certification to bypass mediation
sections.summary: Certification is provided for cases unsuitable for mediation so parties can bypass it and save time and expense.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Sometimes, a dispute may not be suitable for mediation because one side lacks the mental capacity or they may have tried mediation many times and failed or the other party is simply unresponsive or unreasonable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: So, in some these cases, we have decided to provide for a certification where they can bypass to mediation so that effectively it saves time and expense and, in the right cases, you proceed straight to the subsequent process.

sections.label: CRU mediation direction and waiver
sections.summary: CRU may direct parties to CMC mediation but does not mediate; pre-filing mediation for CDRT claims may be waived.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: CRU may, even, at that stage direct parties to attend mediation at CMC, but CRU themselves do not carry out the mediation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: The requirement of pre-filing mediation for CDRT claims may be waived, if the frontline officers assess that it is not suitable for the reasons that I have outlined earlier.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Well, let me start by saying that first of all, the Mediation Direction is not onerous.

sections.label: Consequences for mediation non-attendance
sections.summary: Deliberately not showing up or leaving mediation without permission is an offence, with consequences from advisory to composition.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Having said all that, if you do not show up deliberately or if you leave the mediation session halfway through without permission, then a direction can be issued and that is an offence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Consequences can range from an advisory to a warning or to more serious enforcement actions, such as a composition.

sections.label: CDRT mandatory treatment order power
sections.summary: Empowering the CDRT to make an MTO in civil proceedings tackles root causes early, such as underlying psychiatric conditions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Empowering the CDRT to make an MTO in civil proceedings with the constraints that I had set out earlier, allows the root cause of the issue to be tackled early on and upstream, if the hoarding behaviours, for example, stems from an underlying psychiatric condition.

sections.label: MTO framework unreasonable interference
sections.summary: The MTO framework under new section 12A applies only if a person caused unreasonable interference to his neighbour.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: The MTO framework under the new section 12A applies only if a person has caused unreasonable interference to his neighbour.

sections.label: MTO duration limit
sections.summary: The duration of an MTO depends on the case context and circumstances but cannot exceed 36 months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: The specific duration of an MTO for any given case will, of course, depend on the context and the circumstances of the case, but it cannot exceed 36 months.

sections.label: CDRT claims filed yearly
sections.summary: CDRT claims averaged 88 per year from January 2016 to December 2019 and 205 per year from January 2020 to December 2023.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: From January 2016 to December 2019, an average of 88 CDRT claims were filed each year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: From January 2020 to December 2023, that number went up to 205 CDRT claims each year.

sections.label: Excessive noise CDRT claims
sections.summary: From January 2020 to December 2023, 529 claims, or 64% of total claims filed, involved a complaint on excessive noise.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: For the four-year period of January 2020 to December 2023, 529 claims or 64% of total claims filed involved a complaint on excessive noise.

sections.label: Compliance bond landlord involvement
sections.summary: The enhancement brings the compliance bond mechanism forward one step and sets out a clearer process for landlord involvement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Today, if the tenant does not comply with the first order, the CDRT can already make the second order against the tenant called a special direction and at that stage, the landlord can be asked to put up a compliance bond and the landlord must ensure that the tenant complies with this second order.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: So, the enhancement that we are now making, adds on to this – it does not introduce anything that is new but adds on to this, by bringing that step forward – the compliance bond mechanism is now brought forward by one step and we set out a clearer process of how landlords will then be involved.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: If the landlord had been notified that his tenant is engaging in acts of nuisance and does not do anything and the matter is then taken to the CDRT, the CDRT can, at that stage, make a compliance order against the landlord together with the first order against the tenant.

sections.label: Consent for improved outcomes
sections.summary: They looked at this and felt that requiring consent would give the best chance of improved outcomes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: The short point is, we did look at this and we felt that requiring consent would give the best chance of improved outcomes.

sections.label: Costs orders and CRU
sections.summary: The court is given flexibility on costs orders, and CRU does not intend to seek costs against the resident.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: In such a case, we wanted to give the court hearing the case flexibility in deciding where costs should follow the event and to make the appropriate costs orders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: I want to assure Ms Lim that it is not CRU's intention to seek costs against the resident.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: So, there will be no cost recovery as such, as she had put it in her speech.

sections.label: CDRT amendments and commencement
sections.summary: The Bill applies only from the time the Act is operational, so later amendments are not imposed mid-process.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: If you are halfway through a CDRT process and it is unfair to then impose, after you have started the case, amendments that have been brought in subsequently, then we will not do so.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: So, in fact, the Bill provides for it to be applicable only from the time the Act is operational.

sections.label: Implementation by first half
sections.summary: The plan is to implement by the first half of next year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: I think Ms Sim Ann said the first half of next year and that is the plan as well.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: We intend to do so by the first half of next year.
